name: High-CO2 gas field development with reinjection
principle: A gas field whose gas is largely CO2 is produced with CO2 removed offshore, usually by membranes, and the separated CO2 is compressed and reinjected into a depleted field instead of venting. PETRONAS Kasawari is the reference: a fixed platform bridge-linked to the central processing platform removes CO2, a pipeline carries it to the depleted M1 field and the gas is stored there.

process_steps.name: Sour gas from wells to central processing platform
CO2 removal with membranes and low-pressure booster compression
Subsea CO2 pipeline to depleted field

suppliers.name: Baker Hughes
suppliers.product: gas turbine compressor trains (PGT25+ / PGT25 DLE), two trains each for booster and reinjection

performance.basis: Kasawari project; 71 to 76 Mt over the project life reported

source.note: Oil & Gas Journal, PETRONAS takes FID for offshore Malaysia CCS

performance.basis: Kasawari, Block SK316, about 200 km offshore Bintulu, Sarawak

source.note: Oil & Gas Journal, PETRONAS takes FID for offshore Malaysia CCS
Hydrocarbon Engineering, Baker Hughes to supply technology for offshore CCS facilities, 6 January 2023

reference_plants.name: PETRONAS Kasawari CCS (Block SK316, offshore Sarawak)
reference_plants.status: FID 20 October 2022; the Kasawari gas field began production in August 2024, but CO2 injection had not started as of April 2026 — PETRONAS said on 1 April 2026 it is looking to bring the first CO2 injection forward to as early as 2027, from a previous projection of end-2029/early 2030; the 2025 and end-2025 start-up dates cited in earlier sources did not materialise

source.note: The Star, PETRONAS seeks to bring forward first CO2 injection at Kasawari to 2027, 1 April 2026 (read 28 October 2026); FID from Oil & Gas Journal

advantages: Keeps CO2 out of the atmosphere while a high-CO2 field is commercial
Reuses depleted field as the store
limitations: Large, heavy offshore platform (14,000 t topside, 15,000 t jacket) in 108 m of water
